clue.text: A feature on a plain canopy

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the feature with its article comes after the word for plain

parts.note: plain in the sense of bare or unadorned, as a bald statement is
a facial feature, here the chin

explanation.surface: Someone points out a detail standing on an open plain.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so the article and the facial feature follow the word for plain. A baldachin is a ceremonial covering over a throne or altar.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldachin is an ornamental cloth or structure held over an altar or dignitary as a covering.

clue.text: Dashing young men, lustful and inflamed

parts.note: bloods are fashionable, spirited young men about town
hot means full of desire

explanation.surface: Flashy young men described as lecherous and fired up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodshot eyes are red and irritated, the vessels swollen.

clue.text: Race in one game leads to another

indicators.note: in says the race goes inside the card game

parts.note: loo is an old card game
the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Gambling on one race leads a punter on to the next game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the race inside the card game. Lotto is a numbers game like bingo, hence 'another' game.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance where numbers drawn are matched on cards, a further game beside loo.

clue.text: Copyright vermouth if it's an appetising drink

parts.note: to ape someone is to copy them
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A protected brand of vermouth is touted as a drink to whet the appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copyright' splits into 'Copy' and 'right'. Gin and It is a British pub drink of gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Graduate as footballer

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: half of the word back is BA, the letters after a graduate's name

explanation.surface: A university leaver turns out as a football player.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, taken as wordplay, gives the clue word. BA (Bachelor of Arts) is half of BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-back plays between the forwards and the full-backs in football or rugby.

clue.text: Awful barney not far away

indicators.note: awful suggests the word barney is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dreadful row breaks out close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: A barney is British slang for a noisy quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, within a short distance.

clue.text: Weeded round first of the seedlings, then watered

indicators.note: round says the word for weeded is wrapped about the letter that follows

parts.note: to hoe a bed is to clear it of weeds

indicators.note: first of asks for only the opening letter of the word seedlings

explanation.surface: A gardener weeds around young plants and then gives them a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts S, the first letter of 'seedlings' ('first of'), inside HOED.
explanation.definitionFit: To hose plants is to spray them with water from a hosepipe.

clue.text: Old city king in country dance gets a cheer

indicators.note: in says the city and the king go inside the dance

parts.note: the hay is an old English country dance with weaving figures
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler joins a rustic dance and is greeted with applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the city and the king inside the dance; 'gets' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurray is a shout of joy or approval, an exclamation of applause.

clue.text: Grave repulse, perhaps involving the church

indicators.note: involving says the rearranged letters take in the abbreviation for church
perhaps says the word repulse is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A serious rebuff, possibly concerning the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes SEPULRE; 'involving' then wraps it round the church's abbreviation. 'Grave' is a noun, a tomb, not 'serious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a tomb, a burial place cut in rock or built of stone.

clue.text: Snake ignoring meat a nymph left

indicators.note: ignoring says the meat and the article are left out of the snake's name

parts.note: the hamadryad is another name for the king cobra
ham is meat from a pig's thigh

explanation.surface: A snake that won't eat flesh leaves a spirit of the woods behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes HAM and A from HAMADRYAD; 'left' says what remains. A hamadryad is also a tree nymph, so the answer is nearly the snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree spirit of Greek myth, one of the minor female deities of nature.

clue.text: Take more money, though not allowed to advertise.

parts.note: a ball or a player ruled out is not allowed
to sell a product is to promote it, as in a hard sell

explanation.surface: A shop takes more cash despite being banned from advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsell rivals is to make greater sales and so earn bigger takings than they do.

clue.text: A prize waste

parts.note: a trophy is a cup or award won as a prize

explanation.surface: A complaint that some award is a pointless extravagance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waste' is a verb here, to waste away.
explanation.definitionFit: To atrophy is to wither or shrink through disuse, which is wasting away.

clue.text: Red-hot incendiary burns piece of clothing

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a stretch of letters lifted out of the clue's opening words

explanation.surface: A firebomb so hot that it scorches part of someone's garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'reD-HOT Incendiary'; 'burns' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by Hindu men in India, a garment.

clue.text: A bad ball bowled out Captain ..Reece, for one

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

indicators.note: out signals the words a bad ball are put out of order

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a poor delivery dismisses a batsman called Captain Reece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A BAD BALL into ABBALLAD, after B. The Bab Ballads are W. S. Gilbert's comic verses; 'Captain Reece' is one of them, not a cricketer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert's comic poem about the kindly commander of the Mantelpiece is one of his collected humorous verses.

clue.text: Measure appropriate for Londoners

definitions.meaning: a length of one twelfth of a foot, divided in two
Cockney rhyming slang: the phrase rhymes with pinch, so it means to steal

explanation.surface: A ruling on which unit of measurement suits people in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it; here 'pinch' (steal) becomes this phrase. 'appropriate' is a verb, to take.
explanation.definitionFit: Half an imperial inch is a small length, and to Cockneys it also means to steal, by rhyme with pinch.

clue.text: It takes charge when, say, loaded with drink

indicators.note: say signals that the word for loaded is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: laden means loaded or weighed down
a jar is British slang for a drink, as in a quick jar at the pub

explanation.surface: Someone takes command when, so to speak, drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes charge' suggests leadership, but the device stores electric charge. A Leyden jar is an early capacitor, named after the Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leyden jar was the first device to store static electricity, a glass jar foiled inside and out.

clue.text: Haggard girl married to Noah's boy

parts.note: She is the novel by H. Rider Haggard, named for its heroine Ayesha

explanation.surface: A worn-out young woman weds the son of the ark-builder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' is the novelist, not 'worn out'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the ark-builder had three sons: Shem, Ham and Japheth.

clue.text: One may be entranced by his performance

definitions.text: One may be entranced by his performance

parts.words: One may be entranced by his performance
parts.note: entranced reads as delighted, but means literally put into a trance by a hypnotist's act

explanation.walkthrough: The subject is literally put in a trance, not charmed. Mesmer was an 18th-century pioneer of hypnotism.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesmerist is a hypnotist, who puts subjects into a trance on stage.

clue.text: Good place for a proclamation supported by 24

definitions.text: Good place for a proclamation supported by 24

parts.words: Good place for a proclamation supported by 24
parts.note: news is shouted from the roof, idiomatically, and a roof rests on its end walls, the answer to 24 across

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is 'to proclaim from the housetops'. 24 across is GABLE, the end wall a roof sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: The roof of a house is where, in the idiom, news is shouted to everyone, and it rests on a gable.

clue.text: Visual aid for agent. on schooner, perhaps

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
a schooner is a tall glass for sherry or beer

explanation.surface: An optical device for a secret agent aboard a sailing ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooner' suggests the ship, but it is a drinking glass. In a down clue 'on' puts SPY above GLASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope for seeing distant things.

clue.text: "All is but —: renown and grace is dead" (Macbeth)

definitions.text: All is but —: renown and grace is dead" (Macbeth)

parts.words: All is but —: renown and grace is dead" (Macbeth)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing word is Macbeth's dismissive name for worldly things after Duncan's murder

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth, Act 2 Scene 3: 'All is but toys: renown and grace is dead.' The dash marks the word to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth calls all life's honours mere trifles, playthings of no worth, once the king is dead.

clue.text: Squeeze out a wet cloth

definitions.meaning: to press together into less space
a pad of soaked cloth pressed on the body to ease pain or swelling

explanation.surface: Instructions to wring out a damp flannel.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means press tight; as a noun it is a soaked pad applied to an injury.

clue.text: Bed with heavyweight cloth

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
a ton is a great weight

explanation.surface: A bed made up with thick fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is a fabric woven from the fibre of the cotton plant.

clue.text: Let down girl over guitar

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the girl's name sits above the instrument

parts.note: Di is short for the girl's name Diana
the lute is a stringed instrument in the same family as the guitar

explanation.surface: A girl feels disappointed after playing her guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let down' looks like 'disappoint' but means weaken, as by watering down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilute is to thin or weaken a liquid by adding water.

clue.text: Verses for jogging

parts.note: jogging means jogging the memory, not running: rhymes learnt to help recall facts

explanation.walkthrough: 'jogging' suggests running, but the verses jog the memory, like 'Thirty days hath September'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are memory aids, often little rhymes, that help someone recall facts.

clue.text: Kind of suit for an officer

definitions.meaning: in bridge, hearts and spades are the higher-scoring suits
an army officer ranking above a captain

explanation.surface: A type of uniform meant for a military officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' suggests clothing, but it is a bridge suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, spades and hearts are the senior suits; in the army, the rank above captain.

clue.text: Pointed wall for film actor

definitions.meaning: the triangular upper part of a wall at the end of a ridged roof
Clark ..., Hollywood star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A sharply angled wall reserved for a movie star.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the triangular end wall under a pitched roof, and the surname of the Hollywood star Clark.

clue.text: The nawab is mad, Sir

indicators.note: mad suggests the word nawab has gone wild and scrambled its letters

explanation.surface: A remark that the Indian prince has gone crazy, addressed to a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: A nawab is an Indian Muslim prince. Bwana is Swahili for master, used to address a man like 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: In East Africa it was a respectful form of address for a man, meaning master.

clue.text: It's part of a taboo in self-defence

indicators.note: part of says the first word becomes part of, placed within, the word for a taboo

parts.note: juju is a West African fetish, and by extension a ban or taboo attached to it

explanation.surface: A claim that some forbidden thing belongs within the martial arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' places the clue's opening word inside the word for a taboo, after its third letter; 'in' just links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jujitsu is a Japanese martial art of unarmed combat, a system of fighting off attackers.

clue.text: Thalia moving about married women's apartments

indicators.note: moving about says the letters of the name and the abbreviation are shifted around

explanation.surface: The Muse Thalia flits around the rooms where wives live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving about' rearranges THALIA plus M. In an ancient Greek house the thalamus was the inner chamber kept for the women.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Greek houses these inner chambers were the quarters set aside for the household's women.

clue.text: Show film again about the railwaymen's return

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters

indicators.note: return says the union's initials are turned to run backwards

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A cinema screens a documentary again about the rail union's comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the union's initials around to make RUN. 'film' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To rerun a film is to screen it a second time, a repeat showing.

clue.text: Unimportant person may be taken on board thus casually

definitions.text: Unimportant person may be taken on board thus
definitions.meaning: in chess a pawn, the humblest piece, may be captured in passing by a pawn alongside

explanation.surface: A minor figure might be given a passing welcome aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unimportant person' is a pawn and 'board' the chessboard, where a pawn may be taken by this special capture.
explanation.definitionFit: French for in passing, it names a chess capture of a pawn and also means by the way, incidentally.
